Three blocking acceptance-bound contract defects remain. The semantic validator can record contradictory lifecycle facts, exact subject/revision/relation identities are not uniquely bound, and TypeScript accepts a timestamp rejected by both the wire schema checker and Python. These defects affect the portable public contract that T02 must persist, so approval cannot be deferred to T02 without freezing ambiguous or false provenance semantics.

findings.title: Known-event relation rules accept and require provenance facts that contradict the recorded lifecycle outcome
findings.reproduction: At exact candidate 0cdc367a68195a2360d3d8efc23da137bf0e9790, load packages/contracts/provenance/fixtures/valid-source-acquired-event.v1.json through either generated runtime. Change type to org.research-observatory.entity.invalidated.v1, activityType to invalidation, status to denied, move the fixture output into inputs, clear outputs, and retain wasAssociatedWith plus a wasInvalidatedBy relation for that input. provenanceEventErrors/provenance_event_errors returns no errors. The accepted record therefore says the invalidation was denied while asserting the W3C PROV fact that the entity was invalidated by the denied activity. The same result occurs for failed and cancelled because semanticErrors/_semantic_errors selects wasInvalidatedBy solely from knownActivity === invalidation, independent of status. Conversely, retain the successful source-acquisition fixture and append a well-shaped wasInvalidatedBy relation targeting its newly generated output; both runtimes again return no errors, so one event can say the source was successfully acquired and invalidated by the same non-invalidation activity. Inspection shows the same role gap for other optional relations: used can target outputs, wasGeneratedBy and wasAttributedTo can target inputs, and wasDerivedFrom direction/self-relations are not constrained. These are false or contradictory scholarly lineage facts, not adjacent hardening, and violate the approved requirement for valid success/failure/denial/cancellation behavior and exact W3C PROV-aligned reconstruction.
findings.required_remediation: Make known-event semantic validation status- and role-aware in the schema annotations and both generated runtimes. A failed, denied, or cancelled invalidation attempt must not assert wasInvalidatedBy; either use the approved attempted-operation relation shape or introduce an authority-compatible outcome event vocabulary. For every known event, restrict used to exact inputs, wasGeneratedBy and wasAttributedTo to exact outputs, wasInvalidatedBy to successful invalidation inputs only, and wasDerivedFrom to a non-self output-to-input direction with the intended activity. Reject contradictory extra relations while leaving structurally valid unknown future types storable and uninterpreted. Add table-driven TypeScript and Python parity tests for succeeded, failed, denied, and cancelled shapes, plus negative fixtures for each wrong-role and contradictory relation, before T02 persists this contract. Update the evidence claims to the remediated candidate rather than treating later ledger validation as the fix.

findings.title: Subject and relation endpoints do not bind one exact immutable entity revision
findings.reproduction: At the exact candidate, replace the valid fixture subject's terminal UUID with another valid UUIDv7 that appears nowhere in inputs or outputs while keeping the project prefix; both runtimes return no errors because event-project-and-subject-match checks only startsWith(project/<projectid>/). Duplicate an existing relation object, including its relationId; both runtimes still return no errors because relation identities are never checked for uniqueness. Finally construct a valid document.parsed event with two input entries sharing one entityId but carrying different revisionId values and provide only one used relation for that entityId. Python provenance_event_errors returns an empty tuple, and the equivalent TypeScript logic has the same set/lookup behavior: entity-references-are-unique compares entityId:revisionId pairs, while all relation completeness and closure checks discard revisionId and match only entityId. The one relation therefore purports to bind two distinct immutable revisions. A subject kind can likewise differ from the referenced entityKind. T02 cannot recover which immutable revision an accepted relation meant, and repeated relation identities create a persistence/idempotency collision at the exact boundary T01 is required to define.
findings.required_remediation: Define and enforce an unambiguous identity model before persistence. Bind subject project, kind, and terminal identity to the exact intended entity reference in the event. Require relationId uniqueness and reject identity collisions appropriate to the global UUIDv7 namespace. Most importantly, make every relation endpoint identify one exact entity revision, either by carrying the governed revision identity/composite reference or by enforcing a one-to-one entity identifier invariant that still supports legitimate revision-to-revision transformations under ADR-0024. Relation completeness must be evaluated against that exact reference rather than an entityId set. Add matching schema documentation plus TypeScript/Python tests for an unbound subject, subject-kind mismatch, duplicate relation IDs with identical and different facts, two revisions sharing a stable entity ID, and a valid revision-to-revision transformation.

findings.title: The generated TypeScript timestamp boundary disagrees with the wire schema and Python runtime
findings.reproduction: At the exact candidate, set the valid fixture event time and relation times to 0000-01-01T00:00:01.000Z and the activity start to 0000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z. TypeScript provenanceEventErrors returns an empty array because JavaScript Date accepts year zero and round-trips it. Python provenance_event_errors returns calendar errors for the event, activity, and all relations because datetime.strptime rejects year zero. Draft202012Validator with FormatChecker also rejects every year-zero date-time under the schema's format=date-time authority. Thus the public schema and Python Core reject bytes that the generated TypeScript decoder accepts and can canonicalize; the contract and evidence claim cross-language/schema parity that does not exist.
findings.required_remediation: Use one explicitly documented, schema-compatible UTC instant range and identical calendar validation in the schema, TypeScript, and Python templates. Exclude year zero consistently if the Draft 2020-12/RFC 3339 format boundary remains authoritative, or adopt a validator that all three authorities accept without weakening the current millisecond-Z canonical form. Add a cross-language negative fixture for year zero and boundary fixtures for the minimum/maximum supported instant, asserting identical decode results, canonical bytes, and record hash behavior.
